notes.claim: Coordinates are written alphabetically, so x comes before y, and Bitesize's memory aid is to go along the hallway before going up the stairs.
Oak National Academy lists confusing the x-axis and y-axis, and so counting along the wrong axis, as a mistake pupils might make.
Oak suggests marking the axes clearly on the grid with arrows or labels, and counting along the x-axis and then the y-axis to find a point's coordinates.
Big Ideas Math asks how the points (-3, 1) and (1, -3) differ in location, which puts the swapped-order slip in front of the learner.
